Address: Amos Bird Division.
Submitted by: Tungyueh Road.
P. Y. Koo.

INDUSTRIAL DISPUTE.

Some 60 workers in the employ of the Borden Egg Company, 2 Tungyueh Road, were dismissed by their management on November 7, 1941 owing to shortage of eggs and difficulty in shipping. The management agreed to grant a discharging allowance of half a month's wages and allowances, for every year's service; but the workers were not satisfied and refused to accept the money.

Three workers' representatives, namely Peng Chao Dah (彭朝大), Bien Teh Chwen (卞德春) and Chu Yeh Teh (朱一德), called in the office of the Industrial and Social Division at 9 a.m. November 18, and submitted a petition requesting mediation.

Mr. T. H. Pond, acting manager, was interviewed in the Division office the same afternoon. He stated that the Company had tried its best to maintain the workers' livelihood in the face of slack business during the last six months. Upon instructions from the New York Head Office, the local offices decided to declare a state of suspension, and pay off the workers. The Company, he continued, was generously granting a discharging allowance based on the years of service, and therefore refused to make any further increase. After consideration, he agreed to grant a further concession by paying workers' wages and allowances up to the end of November.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH NOV 26 1941）

At 10 a.m. November 19, the workers' representatives called in the Division office again. They were informed of the firm attitude of their management, and persuaded to accept the discharging allowance generously granted by the management. They requested the Industrial Relations Officer to make a further effort to negotiate with the management for payment of the December wages, and the annual bonus of one month's wages for this year.

Mr. Pond was again consulted in his office the same morning. He agreed to pay one month's additional wages (excluding allowances) as annual bonus for this year, but refused to pay wages for December.

The workers' representatives were informed of the further concessions granted by the management. They were then satisfied, the following being the final terms of settlement:-

地址：阿摩司路分部。
提交人：通岳路。
顾品一 (P. Y. Koo)。

劳资纠纷。

受雇于通岳路2号博登蛋品公司的约60名工人，因鸡蛋短缺及运输困难，于1941年11月7日被资方解雇。资方同意按每服务一年支付半个月工资及津贴作为遣散费；但工人对此不满，拒绝接受该款项。

三名工人代表，即彭朝大、卞德春和朱一德，于11月18日上午9时前往工业社会科办公室，提交请愿书请求调解。

当日下午，代理经理 T. H. Pond 先生在该科办公室接受了问询。他表示，在过去六个月生意清淡期间，公司已尽力维持工人生计。根据纽约总部的指示，本地办事处决定宣布停工状态，并结清工人工资。他接着说，公司正慷慨地根据服务年限发放遣散费，因此拒绝进一步增加金额。经考虑后，他同意再作让步，将工人的工资和津贴支付至11月底。

（印：上海公共租界警务处 特别分部 1941年11月26日）

11月19日上午10时，工人代表再次来到该科办公室。他们被告知资方态度坚决，并被劝告接受资方慷慨提供的遣散费。他们请求劳资关系官员继续努力与资方谈判，要求支付12月份工资以及本年度相当于一个月工资的年终奖金。

同日上午，再次在其办公室咨询了 Pond 先生。他同意支付相当于一个月工资的额外款项（不含津贴）作为本年度年终奖金，但拒绝支付12月份工资。

工人代表获悉资方作出的进一步让步。随后他们表示满意，最终和解条款如下：

Mr. Poltere attended Dr. Horst Lance, M.D. and
was certified to be suffering from bruises and scratching
of left knee, right elbow and in the region of the right
shoulder bone.
At 7.15 a.m. 25/4/40 about 200 strikers gathered
outside Yangtzepoo Police Station and demanded the
release of the six male strikers held in custody. Four
females representing the strikers were invited into the
station to discuss the situation with Mr. H.H. Cameron,
manager of Borden & Company, who informed them that
their demands were preposterous and could not be granted,
but at the same time he added that minor concessions
would be considered providing the strikers resumed work.
These terms were rejected by the strikers, Mr. Cameron
then declared that the factory would be closed until
Monday the 29/4/40 and informed the strikers' represen-
tatives that those wishing to resume work on that day
could do so unconditionally.
The strikers dispersed quietly from outside
the station and no untoward incident occurred.
Mr. Poltere after consulting with Mr. Cameron
stated that he did not consider it would be in the best
interests of the company to prefer a charge of assault
against the detained strikers and requested that they be
released. They were released with a caution at 7 p.m.
25/4/40.
The strikers' representatives deny having any
labour or political affiliations.

波尔泰雷先生在与卡梅伦先生协商后表示，他认为对被拘留的罢工者提出袭击指控不符合公司的最佳利益，并要求释放他们。他们于1940年4月25日晚7时被予以警告后释放。

The persons arrested claimed to be workers of the Borden Company Factory, and gave the following particulars regarding their identity:-

3. 吳金根（Woo Ching Keng），27岁，浦东人，居住于浦东。
4. 朱根泉（Tsu Keng Zien），27岁，浦东人，居住于浦东。
5. 王志清（Wong Tse Ching），23岁，浦东人，居住于浦东。
6. 沈之龍（Sung Yuen Loong），32岁，崇明人，居住于浦东。

经讯问得知，在上周一，即1940年4月22日，博登工厂（腾越路2号）一楼的搬运部召开了一次会议，期间工人们决定提出以下要求：-

1) 每日工资统一增加80%。
2) 每月发放12.00元的米贴，且即使米价下跌或逢节假日，该津贴也不得减少。

档案

Following the meeting, referred to above,
operation of the factory continued smoothly until
the morning of April 24, when the workers, a large
number of whom reside in Pootung, failed to cross
the river when work was due to begin.    Because
of this the management sent a Chinese representative
to Pootung in order to persuade the employees to
resume work.

On arrival in Pootung, the representative of
the management conferred with the workers in the
office of the Standard Oil Company Workers' Union.
At this conference, the employees were urged to
resume their duties and were told that if they did
so the management might consider certain of their
demands.    The workers, however, appointed five
representatives to deliver a letter to the manage-
ment wherein was contained the set of demands referred
to above.    Tsu Chia Kwei, one of those arrested
by the Police on the morning of April 25, was amongst
the representatives who submitted the demands.

Tsu Chia Kwei maintains that he does not know
the names of the other four representatives, stating
that they are workers in the Porters' Department on
the ground floor of the factory, whereas he is em-

在上述会议之后，工厂运作一直平稳，直到4月24日上午，许多居住在浦东的工人未能在工作开始时渡江上班。因此，管理层派遣一名中方代表前往浦东，劝说雇员复工。

抵达浦东后，管理层代表在美孚石油公司（Standard Oil Company）工会办事处与工人进行了会谈。在此次会谈中，敦促雇员恢复职务，并告知如果他们这样做，管理层可能会考虑他们的部分要求。然而，工人们指派了五名代表向管理层递交一封信函，其中包含了上述一系列要求。4月25日上午被警方逮捕的朱家奎（Tsu Chia Kwei）即是提交要求的代表之一。

朱家奎坚称他不知道其他四名代表的姓名，称他们是工厂一楼搬运部的工人，而他受雇于楼上的冷藏部。

On the morning of April 25, 1940, the workers
from Footung crossed the river and together with
the employees who live on the Settlement side of the
river, gathered outside the factory, refusing to
resume work until they had received a reply to
their demands.    A short while later, an American
employee of the factory, Mr. I. FOLTERE, arrived in
his motor-car and attempted to drive through the
gates leading to the factory.    An attempt was made
to prevent him from entering and while making this
attempt it is understood that he was assaulted.
This assault resulted in the arrest of the six men,
mentioned in the first paragraph of this report,
all of whom deny having any labour or political
affiliations.

The management have stated that they will not
re-open the factory until Monday, 29th April, when
providing the employees resume work unconditionally,
certain minor concessions may be granted them.

（批：A.O.D. Yangtzikoo.）

1940年4月25日上午，来自浦东的工人渡江，与居住在租界一侧的雇员一起在工厂外聚集，拒绝复工，直到他们的要求得到答复。不久后，该工厂的一名美籍雇员I. 福尔特雷（I. FOLTERE）先生驾车抵达，试图驱车穿过通往工厂的大门。有人试图阻止他进入，据悉在此过程中他遭到袭击。此次袭击导致本报告第一段提到的六名男子被捕，他们均否认有任何劳工或政治背景。

管理层已声明，在4月29日（星期一）之前不会重新开工，届时如果雇员无条件复工，可能会给予他们某些微小的让步。

（批注：杨树浦行动官（A.O.D. Yangtzikoo）。）
